summary: A legislator who took her late husband's seat brought her sixth-grade daughter to do schoolwork in her Capitol office.
realLife: A Minnesota representative, a teacher who succeeded her late husband, kept her twelve-year-old daughter with her at the Capitol instead of leaving her at home about a hundred miles away. She wove lessons into long days. She said they spent more time together than many mothers and preteens.
gates: A seat is held far from the household's town.
A child under fourteen is in the household.
inGame: A child at home, a legislature sitting away from home and the player's office as a place can carry it.

turns.what: The child stays with a grandparent at home.
turns.writesBack: A kin tie used for care; less time with the child.

turns.what: The child comes only for the last weeks of the session.
The child tires of the Capitol and asks to go home.
turns.writesBack: A talk scene; the parent considers a move home.
